35.34118,-79.40008: Alston House. Philip Alston's Whigs were defeated there by David Fanning's Tories, 1781. Later the home of Benj. Williams, Governor, 1800-02. Is 9 1/2 mi. N.
Benjamin Williams. Four times Governor; Revolutionary officer; congressman. Grave is 9 1/2 miles north.
35.34524,-79.41616: Plank Road. This street is the route of the Fayetteville-to-Salem plank road, a toll road 129 miles long, built 1849-54.
35.3471,-79.41843: Buggy Company. Thomas B. Tyson & W. T. Jones's factory produced horse-drawn vehicles sold across South, 1850s to 1920s. At peak made 3000 per year. Stood here.
35.3472,-79.41849: James McConnell 1887 1917. World War I soldier; aviator. Flew for France in Lafayette Escadrille. Killed in action, March 19, 1917. Lived 1 mi. W.
35.35985,-79.43654: Tory Rendezvous. Before going to battle of Moore's Creek Bridge, Feb., 1776, Tories of this area met in Cross Hill, at Alexander Morrison's home, 125 yards S.W.
